title: WHO-format Medical Certificate of Cause of Death
description: Output contract for the conversion module. Written to stay inside the limits of Anthropic constrained decoding: no recursion, no numeric or string constraints, no external $ref, additionalProperties false everywhere, array minItems only 0 or 1. Anything those would have enforced is checked in src/validate.py instead, which can explain a violation where a schema can only reject one.

record_id.description: Identifier of the record being certified, copied verbatim from the input.

assessment.description: certifiable: the record supports a cause-of-death chain. insufficient_information: it does not, and guessing would be worse than declining. out_of_scope: an external cause, an undetermined manner of death, or a case needing forensic expertise.

decline_reason.description: Required when assessment is not certifiable; null otherwise.

part1.description: The causal chain. Index 0 is line 1a, the immediate cause; the last entry is the originating condition and sits on the lowest used line. One condition per line, most immediate first. Empty when assessment is not certifiable.

part2.description: Other significant conditions contributing to death but not part of the Part I sequence.

certified_term.description: The condition as it should appear on the certificate: a specific, unabbreviated diagnosis. Not a mode of dying.

evidence_field.description: Which input field the evidence came from. Use case_narrative for the simulated teaching scenarios, which arrive as a single narrative rather than the 14-field record structure. Use none only when basis is clinical_inference or absent.

evidence_span.description: A VERBATIM fragment of the named field supporting this condition. Copied exactly, not paraphrased; it is checked by string comparison against the input. Empty string only when basis is clinical_inference or absent.

basis.description: How the condition was established. explicit_diagnosis: stated as a diagnosis in the record. clinical_inference: not stated, concluded from findings. medication_implied: inferred from a prescription. reported_by_family: stated by a relative rather than clinically documented. absent: named because the chain requires it but the record does not support it.

interval.description: Approximate interval between onset of this condition and death. Must be non-decreasing going down the chain: the immediate cause on 1a began most recently.

value.description: Null when a duration is implied but no number can be supported.

certainty.description: documented: a duration or dates appear in the record. estimated: inferred from the clinical course. unknown: not determinable.

note.description: One sentence for the reviewing physician: what is uncertain and what would resolve it. Length capped by the validator, not here.
